title: Token synchronization for tiered reserved + shared quota windows
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: Customers on mixed plans (reserved pools + pay-as-you-go/shared) occasionally experience unexpected throttles or transient double-bursting around reset boundaries. This happens when tenant-level rolling windows and reserved-pool monthly anchors are not harmonized: tokens consumed against a reserved pool may be incorrectly reported to the tenant ledger at reset, leading to either premature throttling of shared requests or unexpected invoice corrections later.

This ticket designs and implements a token synchronization layer that: (1) aligns soft reset windows between tenant and reserved-pool accounting; (2) debits usage from the correct ledger atomically at rollovers; (3) applies a short soft-staggered cutover to avoid simultaneous high-volume resets across tenants in a pool; and (4) surfaces reconciliation telemetry for automatic correction if drift occurs. The goal is correctness and reduced customer-visible flapping during boundary conditions (month/day/rolling-window boundaries, timezone cutovers, and DST/leap-second anomalies).
acceptance_criteria: No tenant sees >2% unexpected throttles attributable to reset events in canary tests (measured over 72h)
Billing ledger delta between reserved-pool view and tenant view < $0.01 per 100k tokens after scheduled reset for 99.9% of accounts in test harness
End-to-end integration tests that simulate DST, leap-second, and cross-region time skew pass in CI
Canary rollout (5%) with auto-rollback on reconciliation-telemetry spike configured
Operational runbook added to runbooks/quotas with rollback and forensic steps
proposal:
Introduce a thin synchronization service (quota-sync) that sits between the usage ingestor and the billing ledger. It will: 1) maintain an authoritative ephemeral per-tenant 'reset-intent' timestamp computed from tenant config (monthly/day/rolling) and its reserved-pool membership; 2) compute a deterministic soft-stagger offset seeded from tenant-id hash and pool-id to spread cutovers over a configurable jitter window (default 3 minutes); 3) attempt atomic debit operations against reserved-pool ledger first, falling back to tenant shared ledger with circuit-breaker semantics; 4) emit reconciliation events when ledger deltas exceed tolerance and enqueue background reconciliation jobs. This preserves per-request low-latency by doing most work asynchronously, but provides synchronous guarantees around the cutover window to avoid double-debits.

We will also augment the tenant quota API with a read-only "next_cutover" and "cutover_state" field to help the console and SDKs show imminent reset state to customers and SDKs (opt-in beta).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement quota-sync prototype, unit tests, local ledger simulator
Phase 2 (staging): hook into staging ingestion, run 100 synthetic tenants across 3 pools, verify ledgers and telemetry
Phase 3 (canary): deploy to 5% of production pool traffic for 48h with enhanced observability
Phase 4 (gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with two-day intervals and clustering telemetry review between each step
Auto-rollback: on reconciliation error rate > 0.5% or billing delta above threshold revert to previous path and alert on-call
implementation_steps: Spec: create design doc in Confluence outlining state machine and API (assigned to Diego)
Ledger shim: implement 'apply_cutover' atomic operation in ledger service (ENG infra owner PR)
Sync service: build quota-sync microservice with in-memory soft-offset table and durable offset persistence in config-store
Ingress hook: modify usage ingestor to tag events with 'pre_cutover' and 'post_cutover' markers
SDK/Console flag: expose read-only cutover metadata behind feature flag 'quota-cutover-v1'
Testing harness: extend billing-sim to inject DST/leap-second/timewarp events and validate reconciliation jobs
PRs & review: open coordinated PRs across runtime, ledger, ingestor, and console; run cross-team design review
testing_plan: Unit tests for soft-stagger offset generation and deterministic distribution
Integration tests: simulate 1k tenants across 10 pools with randomized request spikes near boundary
Chaos test: introduce simulated ingress lag and region clock skew to verify idempotency and correction path
Billing reconciliation test: nightly job that verifies ledger parity and replays discrepancy scenarios
Performance: measure additional P99 latency on token ingestion (target < 3ms added)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: adding synchronous work on critical ingest path could increase tail latency. Mitigation: keep cutover work async for 99% of requests, only enforce atomic debit during the short pre-cutover window and keep window under 5 minutes.
Risk: incorrect offset distribution could concentrate resets. Mitigation: seeded hashing + telemetry histograms; if hot-spots found, increase jitter window and rotate seed.
Risk: reconciliation flood after outage causing billing noise. Mitigation: rate-limit reconciliation jobs and apply aggregated corrections with audit trail to avoid invoice churn.
Risk: cross-region clock skew. Mitigation: use CRDT-style monotonic counters with authoritative UTC time in control plane and tolerate small negative deltas by deferring non-critical corrections.
notes: Related tickets: ENG-411019 (burst realignment), ENG-101205 (microreset smoothing)
